PFG.thesis_one_line: Retirement plans and asset management for small US employers, earning more each year and priced for slow growth, but tied to stock-market levels.
kill_criteria: Non-GAAP operating EPS ex-significant variances below $2.17 (the 1Q26 level) in any two consecutive quarters.
AUM net cash flow worse than -$10B in two consecutive quarters (2Q26: -$11.1B).
Delinquent problem commercial mortgage loans (consolidated carrying amount) above $500M (now $218.7M at 2026-06-30).
Principal Life Insurance Company statutory RBC ratio below 350% (406% at 2025-12-31), or excess and available capital below $1.0B (now $1.6B).
Full-year 2026 outlook of "9-12% annual non-GAAP operating earnings per diluted share (EPS) growth" or "15-17% non-GAAP ROE" withdrawn or cut.
key_adverse_facts: AUM net cash flow was -$11.1B in 2Q26 (vs -$2.6B) and -$14.4B over the trailing twelve months; no reason disclosed in the release.
Delinquent problem commercial mortgage loans rose to five loans/$218.7M carrying amount (valuation allowance $74.1M) at 2026-06-30 from three loans/$123.7M at 2025-12-31.

GAAP net income attributable to PFG was -1% in 2Q26 ($403.4M vs $406.2M) while non-GAAP operating earnings rose 12%, because of the funds-withheld embedded derivative swing; earnings depend on favourable variable investment income and encaje returns.
data_conflicts: Triage quoted 11.3x forward P/E; my figure is 12.1x on $9.50 2026E operating EPS ex-significant variances (114.77 / 9.50).
Triage listed no red flags; the filings show rising problem mortgage loans and large Q2 AUM outflows.
No numeric guidance is restated in the 1Q26 or 2Q26 releases; the 2026 outlook exists only in the 4Q25 release. FY25 outlook ranges were not obtained, so the FY25 track record is not scored.
PFG.confidence_in_thesis: medium: guidance pace and margins are documented in primary filings, but the Q2 outflow cause, Form 4 pattern and Q2 RBC ratio were not checked; next_earnings_date is an estimate

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for PFG. Reverse DCF (9.5% cost of equity, 3.0% terminal, FCF $1,449M) implies about 3.9% a year free-cash growth for 10 years versus my base of about 6% for free cash and 9% for EPS.

PFG.scenario_basis: Start 2026E operating EPS ex-significant variances $9.50, price $114.77, dividend $3.36 annualised; bear 2029 EPS $8.00 at 9.5x, flat dividend; base +9%/yr to $12.30 at 12.0x, dividend +8%/yr; bull +12%/yr to $13.35 at 13.5x, dividend +10%/yr.

F.thesis_one_line: Sells America's best-selling trucks and work vans; priced as if profits will shrink, though the electric-vehicle losses and special charges remain real.
kill_criteria: Company adjusted FCF below $1.0B in 2H 2026 cumulative (the full-year range "$6.0 billion to $7.0 billion" implies about $5.8B or more).
Full-year 2026 adjusted EBIT range cut below $9.0B (current "Adjusted EBIT of $10.0 billion to $11.0 billion"), or 2027 adjusted EBIT margin below 5%.
Ford Model e quarterly EBIT loss worse than $1.2B (2Q26: -$919M) in two consecutive quarters.
Warranty and field-service accrual (net of recoveries) above $19.0B, or pre-existing warranty revisions above $1.0B in a half-year (H1 2026: $475M).
Company excluding Ford Credit cash below $15B or the regular dividend reduced below $0.15 a quarter.
key_adverse_facts: FY25 pre-tax special items of $17.4B ($16.6B excluding pension/OPEB) produced a GAAP loss of $8.2B against adjusted EBIT of $6.8B; 2Q26 added $4.2B (incl. $3.6B BOSK). TTM GAAP net loss is about $7.4B.

H1 2026 adjusted FCF was only $0.2B versus a full-year guide of $6.0-7.0B, so H2 needs about $5.8-6.8B; adjusted FCF excludes restructuring, funded pension and 'other, net' cash outflows (about $2.15B in FY25, $2.67B in H1 2026) and counts Ford Credit distributions ($1,875M in H1 2026).

1Q26 adjusted EBIT of $3.5B included a one-time $1.3B IEEPA tariff benefit; Ford assumed a $3,805,040,000 DOE note for the Kentucky battery plant on the BOSK exit; warranty accrual $17,571M (consolidated) with up to about $2.0B reasonably possible additional field-action cost.
data_conflicts: Triage cited negative FCF; H1 2026 company adjusted FCF is +$0.2B (GAAP TTM and 1Q26 adjusted FCF were negative).
Triage claim of a dealer class action over warranty reimbursement and Model e losses through 2029 was not found in the 10-Q or releases read.
Triage 6.6x NTM P/E vs my 6.8x on guide-based $1.85 adjusted EPS; adjusted and GAAP EPS diverge massively (FY25 adjusted $1.09 vs GAAP -$2.06).
F.confidence_in_thesis: low-to-medium: guidance raised twice in 2026 and valuation implies little growth, but cyclical, special-item-prone earnings, H2-loaded FCF, and Form 4 and CAM checks not done; next_earnings_date is an estimate

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for F. Reverse DCF (11% cost of equity, 2% terminal): on the dossier's $5.0B normalised adjusted FCF the price implies 0.7% a year, but adjusted FCF excludes about $2.15B (FY25) of pension, restructuring and other cash costs and SBC; on a strict basis (about $3.9B at guide mid) it implies 4.3% a year versus my base of about 4% (about 11% on a $2.4B basis). Restated below -> in line by DVH5, 2026-10-06; verdict unchanged, no margin of safety.

F.scenario_basis: Start 2026E adjusted EPS about $1.85 (guide mid, ex-IEEPA $1.58), price $12.71, dividend $0.60; bear 2029 EPS $1.00 at 6.0x with dividend cut to $0.30; base $2.30 (about $12.5B adjusted EBIT) at 7.0x with $0.60 dividend; bull $3.00 (8% margin) at 8.0x with $0.65 dividend.

KR.thesis_one_line: America's biggest traditional grocer, cheap and buying back shares, but sales are stalling and profit growth is coming only from fewer shares.
kill_criteria: Identical sales without fuel (company definition) below 0.0% for any fiscal quarter, or the "0.2% - 0.8%" full-year range cut again.
Adjusted FIFO operating profit below $1,000M in FQ3 2026 (12 weeks; FQ2 2026: $1,076M), or the full-year range "$5.0 - $5.2 billion" cut below $5.0B.
Full-year adjusted FCF range "$2.7 - $2.9 billion" cut below $2.4B, or net total debt to adjusted EBITDA (consolidated, company definition) above 2.5x after the Giant Eagle deal.
Adjusted EPS range "$5.10 - $5.30" cut, or adjusted EPS growth below +3% in two consecutive quarters with share count falling more than 5%.
Adverse Albertsons ruling above $600M (Delaware Court of Chancery) or opioid settlement cost above the disclosed "up to $1,200" million (states and subdivisions) plus $36M (tribes).
key_adverse_facts: FQ2 2026 adjusted FIFO operating profit fell 1.4% ($1,076M vs $1,091M) and adjusted net earnings fell about 4% (my calculation); adjusted EPS +5% came from an 8.6% lower diluted share count (608M vs 665M).
Full-year 2026 identical sales without fuel guide cut to 0.2%-0.8% from 1.0%-2.0%; FQ2 identical sales 0.2% with 138 bps Inflation Reduction Act drag.
H1 2026 consolidated FCF $648M vs $1,720M; temporary cash investments fell to $1,475M from $4,668M; $1.25B cash Giant Eagle acquisition pending; Albertsons claims a $600M termination fee.
data_conflicts: Triage 10.9x forward P/E vs my 11.3x on the $5.20 guide-mid adjusted EPS; consensus not verified.
Triage did not mention the sales-guide cut, the new CEO reset or the investor update on 2026-10-20.
Adjusted FCF guide ($2.7-2.9B) includes add-backs (opioid, Ocado exit, pension restructuring); FY25 unadjusted FCF was $3,418M vs adjusted $3,868M.
KR.confidence_in_thesis: low-to-medium: guidance and balance sheet are documented in primary filings, but strategy will be reset at the 2026-10-20 investor update; next_earnings_date is an estimate; Form 4 and CAMs not checked

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for KR. Reverse DCF (8.0% cost of equity, 2.5% terminal, adjusted FCF $2.8B) implies about -2.6% a year free-cash growth (-0.7% on $2.4B) versus my base of about +3%; WATCH rests on earnings quality and the near-term strategy reset, not on price.

KR.scenario_basis: Start 2026E adjusted EPS $5.20 (guide mid), price $58.74, dividend $1.56 annualised; bear 2029 EPS $5.00 at 9.5x, flat dividend; base +6%/yr to $6.19 at 11.5x, dividend +10%/yr; bull +9%/yr to $6.73 at 13.0x, dividend +11%/yr.
